intent_en: To illustrate how central banks have significantly lowered interest rates to stimulate the economy, particularly highlighting the sharp decline following the 2008 financial crisis and subsequent further reductions.
previous_intent: To explain how central banks have utilized interest rate cuts to stimulate economic growth, highlighting the sharp decline after the 2008 financial crisis and the continued push toward lower rates.
narration_support: lowering interest rates is a big way central banks try to get the economy moving. It's why they dropped so sharply in 2008. So incredibly they've managed to drop even further.
chart_support: Line chart showing interest rates declining over time from 1991 to 2016, with a sharp drop annotated at the 2008 Financial crisis.
evidence_note: The narration explicitly links rate lowering to economic stimulation and mentions the 2008 drop. The chart visualizes this with a downward trend and a specific annotation for 2008, supporting the narrative of aggressive rate cuts.
